question: Should core expose cross-agent queue and capacity state to agents as a supported scheduling input?
rationale: The backend is available, but who may see other agents' workload and whether capacity is advisory or a supported scheduling contract require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Narrow advisory tool
options.body: Expose policy-filtered lane counts and caller-visible capacity with explicitly non-reserving advisory semantics.

options.title: Operator-only diagnostics
options.body: Keep queue snapshots limited to authenticated CLI/RPC operators and do not expose workload state to agents.

options.title: Stable dispatcher contract
options.body: Define per-agent workload, reservations, and scheduling guarantees as a broader core orchestration API.

recommendation.title: Narrow advisory tool
recommendation.body: Expose policy-filtered lane counts and caller-visible capacity with explicitly non-reserving advisory semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced sessions_spawn, centralized concurrency behavior, and has the strongest recent history on the relevant queue and tool-catalog surfaces.
